claim_text: A PTEN-null patient-derived xenograft was resistant to BYL719 but responded to pan-PI3K inhibition or the BYL719 plus AZD6482 p110-beta combination `pmid-25409150`.
evidence_summary: pmid-25409150 derived a PTEN-null PDX from a nonresponding lung metastasis after BYL719 progression, treated nude-mouse xenografts with BYL719, pan-PI3K inhibitor BKM120, p110-beta inhibitor AZD6482, or combinations, and measured tumor growth plus pAKT/pS6. The PDX resisted BYL719 but responded to BKM120 and BYL719 plus AZD6482. Limitation: one patient-derived model.
reviewer_notes: Directly supported by the normalized full text.

claim_text: PTEN and ESR1 alterations together marked nearly half of profiled progressing cases, showing that resistance can arise through the PI3K pathway, the endocrine-therapy component, or both `pmid-32864625`.
evidence_summary: pmid-32864625 analyzed HR-positive metastatic breast cancer patients treated with alpelisib plus letrozole or exemestane using paired tissue and ctDNA sequencing, resistance/progression endpoints, and ESR1 model testing. PTEN loss and ESR1 activating mutations were present in 15 of 32 paired ctDNA cases and were associated with progression. Limitation: small nonrandomized correlative cohort.

claim_text: A later cohort of patients progressing on alpelisib or inavolisib similarly found acquired PI3K pathway alterations in about half of serial ctDNA cases, including PTEN loss-of-function alterations in 5 of 32 and PTEN alteration in 1 of 8 rapid-autopsy series, but also AKT1, secondary PIK3CA, FGFR, KRAS, and BRAF changes `pmid-37916958`. p110-beta compensation should therefore be described as an important PTEN-linked and adaptive route, not simply as the only downstream escape.
corrected_claim: A later cohort of patients progressing on alpelisib or inavolisib found acquired PI3K pathway alterations in about half of serial ctDNA cases, including PTEN loss-of-function alterations in 5 of 32 and PTEN alteration in 1 of 8 rapid-autopsy series, alongside AKT1, secondary PIK3CA, FGFR, KRAS, and BRAF changes.
evidence_summary: pmid-37916958 used serial ctDNA from 32 alpelisib- or inavolisib-treated HR-positive HER2-negative advanced breast cancer patients plus WES of 100 lesions from 8 rapid autopsies, finding acquired PI3K pathway alterations in 50% of ctDNA cases, PTEN alterations in 5/32 and 1/8 autopsy cases, and other PI3K/MAPK/RTK alterations. Limitation: this paper does not directly test p110-beta compensation.
reviewer_notes: The cohort supports heterogeneity and PTEN as one route, but the p110-beta compensation clause relies on adjacent evidence not cited for this exact claim.

claim_text: IGF1R inhibition disrupted the complex, and either IGF1R or p110-beta inhibition restored BYL719 sensitivity in vitro and improved tumor control in MCF7 xenografts `pmid-27048245`.
evidence_summary: pmid-27048245 generated BYL719-resistant T47D and MCF7 PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer cells, used phosphotyrosine proteomics and co-immunoprecipitation to identify an IGF1R/IRS/p85/p110-beta complex, and tested AEW541 or p110-beta inhibitors with BYL719 in vitro and in MCF7 xenografts. Combination treatment reduced resistant-cell growth and strongly decreased xenograft tumor growth. Limitation: preclinical models only.
reviewer_notes: Supported; the xenograft p110-beta inhibitor was GSK2636771 rather than AZD6482 for tolerability.

claim_text: Non-genetic PTEN inactivation adds another layer: PI3K inhibitor exposure can activate a USP10-GSK3-beta axis that phosphorylates PTEN, blocks dimerization, maintains PIP3 and downstream signaling, and can be countered by USP10 or GSK3-beta suppression in resistant models and patient-derived organoids `pmid-40991650`.
evidence_summary: pmid-40991650 studied breast cancer PDXs, MCF7/T47D resistant models, functional DUB screens, PTEN phosphorylation/dimerization assays, PIP3 and pAKT/pS6 readouts, and PDX-derived organoids. PI3K inhibition promoted GSK3-beta-mediated PTEN Thr366 phosphorylation, impaired PTEN dimerization, maintained PIP3/AKT signaling, and USP10 or GSK3-beta suppression resensitized models/organoids. Limitation: clinical predictive value remains unvalidated.

claim_text: Because PTEN status has been defined by copy number, mutation, protein IHC, and downstream phosphoprotein readouts across studies, later verification should keep baseline PTEN loss, acquired genetic PTEN loss, adaptive p110-beta signaling, and post-translational PTEN inactivation as separate evidence classes `pmid-31859350`.
corrected_claim: PTEN-status comparisons across PI3K inhibitor studies should distinguish genetic loss, protein IHC loss, downstream pathway readouts, and PI3K-beta dependence rather than treating all PTEN-related evidence as one class.
evidence_summary: pmid-31859350 is a narrative biomarker review of ER-positive breast cancer PI3K inhibitor studies; it notes PTEN status was variably defined by allelic or complete PTEN loss, IHC protein expression, and downstream markers such as phosphorylated AKT, with different antibodies and thresholds. Limitation: it does not cover later post-translational PTEN inactivation evidence and is not primary resistance data.
reviewer_notes: The measurement caveat is supported, but this 2019 review cannot support the later post-translational PTEN class named in the exact claim.

claim_text: Systematic resistance work reinforces this caution: PI3K inhibitor escape in breast cancer is heterogeneous, and post-resistance biopsies may show multiple resistance programs rather than one dominant lesion `pmid-27604488`.
evidence_summary: pmid-27604488 performed gain-of-function resistance screens in BYL719-treated breast cancer cells, validation across cell models and inhibitors, and RNA-seq of paired BYL719-treated breast tumor biopsies. Multiple resistance genes and programs, including PIM and AKT-related signals, appeared across post-relapse biopsies. Limitation: only a small number of paired clinical biopsies.
